doc.title: Karolina Strassmayer interviewed by Monk Rowe, May 25, 2023

chapter: Her music, free jazz and playing
title: Avoiding copying and learning to let go
summary: Imitation can get too cute; free playing taught her to relax and trust.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: It’s tempting. It’s tempting, yeah. It’s what my friend Anat Cohen used to call “Neanderthal interaction.”
You sounded just like her too.

So yeah that can get a little too cute. So I try not to go there but sometimes it happens and I don’t think it’s a horrible thing when it happens. You can have a sense of humor about it. I guess when you play free music, or for me actually it’s really helping me to relax about music because you’ve just got to let things go. You can’t control what other people play. When I write a tune and I say I want you to play this chord here and there’s the altered chord and no don’t play that, so you’re much more in control of what happens. But with free music I’ve learned to relax and trust that something is going to happen and it’s not going to be what I think will happen or what I want to happen. I had to learn to just go with that instead of thinking ooh I don’t like this, oh what are they doing. You’ve just got to let go of that and just at any given moment just let go, let go and go forward.
It’s almost like you change your expectations.
